"Possible condition-identifying clues, or none observed"}}, "reports": {"A": "# Visitor Desk Status Note — Ferry Service (as of 15 February 2026)

**Can we advertise a 1 March launch? No.** The 1 March date is a superseded proposal. On 1 February the operator proposed launching passenger service on 1 March, contingent on vessel delivery and operating permission, but on 10 February it withdrew that target after delivery slipped (S1). Advertising a 1 March service would mislead visitors.

**Current position.** The operator's most recent notice names 15 April as the earliest possible passenger launch, still subject to vessel delivery, sea trials and final operating permission (S1). No tickets have been released (S1). As of 14 February, the vessel had not been delivered, and there is no final passenger-service permission, confirmed timetable or booking release; the port log makes no prediction on when these will be completed (S2).

**Important clarification on March sailings.** A 12 February port entry permits non-passenger trial sailings during March (S2). This is a trial authorization only — it does not authorize carrying paying passengers (S2). Staff must not describe these sailings as a passenger service.

**Before accepting bookings, verify:** (1) vessel delivery confirmed; (2) completed trials; (3) final passenger-service permission granted; (4) a confirmed timetable published; and (5) an official ticket/booking release by the operator (S1, S2).

Until all five are confirmed, advise visitors that no launch date is guaranteed.

", "B": "# Visitor Desk Status Note — Ferry Service (as of 15 February 2026)

**No, the new ferry cannot be advertised as available from 1 March.** That date is a withdrawn plan, not a current commitment.

The operator originally proposed launching passenger service on 1 March, but on 10 February it withdrew that target after the vessel delivery slipped and proposed 15 April as the earliest possible launch instead, still subject to delivery, trials and final operating permission (S1). This makes 1 March a superseded plan and 15 April a proposed, conditional date only. No tickets had been released as of 10 February (S1), and there was still no booking release, confirmed timetable, or final passenger-service permission as of 14 February (S2).

What the port log *does* permit is limited: a 12 February entry authorizes non-passenger trial sailings during March (S2). Trial permission is not passenger authorization — it explicitly does not permit carrying paying passengers (S2), and the vessel had not yet been delivered (S2).

**Before accepting or advertising any bookings, verify:**
1. Vessel delivery has occurred.
2. Trials have been completed successfully.
3. Final operating permission for passenger service is in place.
4. A confirmed timetable and ticket release are announced by the operator.

Until all four are confirmed, the desk should describe the service as "planned, date not confirmed" and decline to promise either the 1 March or 15 April date.

*(229 words)*
